title: Lamb Kofta
subtitle: Spiced minced lamb skewers
excerpt: Minced lamb mixed with onion, spices, and fresh herbs, shaped onto skewers and cooked over high heat until charred outside and juicy inside. A staple across the Middle East and South Asia, and an essential for a summer barbecue or grill night.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kofta are spiced meat patties or skewers found across the Middle East, South Asia, Central Asia, and the Balkans. The name comes from the Persian koftan, meaning to grind. Lamb kofta on skewers, grilled over charcoal, are one of the defining dishes of Turkish, Persian, Lebanese, and Pakistani cooking. The spice blend varies by region: cumin and coriander are common to most, while cinnamon and allspice appear in the Lebanese and Levantine versions.

content.text: The mince must be well-chilled before shaping so it holds on the skewer. Do not overwork the mixture or the texture becomes dense. Squeeze out any excess moisture from the grated onion before adding it: too much liquid and the kofta will fall off the skewers as they cook. Rest the shaped kofta in the fridge for at least 30 minutes to firm up before cooking.
Combine all ingredients except the oil in a large bowl. Mix well with your hands for 2 minutes until the mixture is homogeneous. Do not overwork it. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes minimum.

Divide the mixture into 8 portions. Wet your hands and shape each around a metal skewer, squeezing firmly into a sausage shape about 12 cm long. The mixture should cover the skewer evenly without gaps. Refrigerate for 15 more minutes while you heat the grill or griddle.
Cook over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until charred in patches and cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes. Serve with flatbread, yoghurt, and salad.
